title: Understand Your Annual Market Salary Rate: Hourly to Annual Pay Calculator
description: Convert your hourly rate to an annual market salary rate using 38-hour weeks. Includes tax, super, and fortnightly pay estimates based on Fair Work and ATO data.
salarySummary: For a full-time employee on the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, working 38 hours per week, the annual market salary rate is approximately $52,268 before tax and super.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual market salary rate from my hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time role, we assume 38 hours per week. For example, $30 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $59,280 per year. This is your gross annual market salary rate before tax and super.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage ($26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026) is the legal minimum for all employees not covered by an award or agreement. Award rates are higher minimums set for specific industries and occupations. You can check your award using the Fair Work Ombudsman's [pay guides](/blog) to ensure you're being paid correctly.

faqs.q: Is superannuation included in my annual market salary rate?
faqs.a: No, superannuation is paid on top of your salary. The super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings (up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830). So if your annual market salary rate is $60,000, your employer should contribute an additional $7,200 into your super fund.

bodyMarkdown:
## What Is an Annual Market Salary Rate?

Your **annual market salary rate** is the gross yearly pay you would earn if you worked a standard full-time schedule at your current hourly rate. It's a useful benchmark for comparing job offers, negotiating pay, or understanding where you sit relative to industry averages. The Fair Work Ombudsman and the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) provide authoritative data to help you make sense of these figures.

To calculate your annual market salary rate, use the formula:

**Hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

For a full-time employee, we assume 38 hours per week – the standard ordinary hours under most awards and the National Employment Standards. If you work part-time or casual, adjust the weekly hours accordingly.

### Example: National Minimum Wage

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour. For a full-time employee:

- Weekly pay: $26.44 × 38 = $1,004.72
- Fortnightly pay: $1,004.72 × 2 = $2,009.44
- Annual market salary rate: $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,267.84 (approximately $52,268)

If you're a casual employee, you receive a 25% loading instead of paid leave. The casual minimum rate is $33.05 per hour, giving an annual market salary rate of about $65,335.

## Using the Timesheet Calculator

Our [timesheet](/) tool lets you enter your base hourly rate. If you're casual, tick the checkbox to add 25% casual loading on top – never enter a rate that already includes loading. The calculator then shows your annual market salary rate, fortnightly pay, and estimated tax and super.

## Tax on Your Annual Market Salary Rate

Your annual market salary rate is your gross income before tax. The Australian Taxation Office (ATO) applies the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- $0 – $18,200: Nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15c for each $1 over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30c for each $1 over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37c for each $1 over $135,000
- $190,001 and over: $51,420 plus 45c for each $1 over $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (with reductions available for low-income earners).

For example, on an annual market salary rate of $80,000:
- Tax: $4,020 + 30% × ($80,000 - $45,000) = $4,020 + $10,500 = $14,520
- Medicare levy: $80,000 × 2% = $1,600
- Total deductions: $16,120
- Take-home pay: $63,880 per year (about $1,228 per week)

Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide for more detailed estimates.

## Superannuation Is Paid on Top

Your employer must pay superannuation guarantee contributions of 12% of your ordinary earnings, on top of your annual market salary rate. This is not deducted from your pay. The maximum contribution base is $270,830 per quarter.

So if your annual market salary rate is $80,000, your employer adds $9,600 to your super fund. That's separate from your take-home pay.

## Comparing to Market Rates

The ABS Average Weekly Earnings (May 2026) report shows:
- Full-time adult ordinary time earnings: $2,083.70 per week (annualised: $108,352)
- All employees total earnings (including part-time): $1,579.20 per week (annualised: $82,118)

These figures include overtime and bonuses. Your annual market salary rate may differ depending on your industry, experience, and location. Check the Fair Work Ombudsman's [pay guides](/blog) for award-specific minimum rates, or browse our [reference tables](/data) for common roles.

## Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

Many employers pay fortnightly. Your fortnightly gross pay is simply your weekly pay multiplied by two. Using the $80,000 example:
- Weekly: $1,538.46
- Fortnightly: $3,076.92

After tax and Medicare, your fortnightly take-home is about $2,456.

## Important Considerations

- **Award vs minimum wage:** The National Minimum Wage is the floor. Most employees are covered by an award with higher rates. Always check your award.
- **Casual loading:** Casual employees get 25% loading but no paid leave. Use our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page to understand the trade-off.
- **Salary packaging:** If you salary sacrifice, your taxable income reduces, affecting your annual market salary rate comparison. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).
- **HELP loans:** Repayments are additional deductions not shown here.

## Estimating Your Annual Market Salary Rate

To get a quick estimate:
1. Enter your hourly rate in our [timesheet](/).
2. Select casual if applicable (the tool adds 25% loading).
3. View your annual market salary rate, fortnightly pay, tax, and super.

Remember, this is an estimate. Your actual pay may vary due to unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or enterprise agreements. Always refer to your employment contract and the relevant award.

For more on converting between hourly and annual figures, visit our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) guide. To see how your pay compares to typical jobs, check [average pay](/topics/average-pay) or [job pay](/topics/job-pay).
